# SEC TRIBUNAL — PROSECUTION'S BEAR CASE
## In re: INTEL CORP (INTC, CIK 0000050863)

May it please the Tribunal. The Prosecution submits that the evidence on file — the defendant's own SEC-reported figures — demonstrates a company in sustained structural decline. I present five charges.

---

**CHARGE 1: Chronic, Multi-Year Revenue Collapse**

The defendant's top line has shrunk for four consecutive fiscal years: from $79.02B (FY2021) to $63.05B (FY2022, -20.2% YoY), to $54.23B (FY2023, -14.0%), to $53.10B (FY2024, -2.1%), to $52.85B (FY2025, -0.5%) [Exhibit A]. That is a cumulative loss of over $26B in annual revenue — roughly a third of the business — with no fiscal year of growth in the record. Recent quarterly upticks (e.g., $16.13B in Q ended 2026-06-27) do not erase four straight years of contraction.

**CHARGE 2: Gross Margin Destruction**

Gross margin has cratered from 55.4% in FY2021 to 42.6% (FY2022), 40.0% (FY2023), and 32.7% (FY2024), with only a modest recovery to 34.8% in FY2025 [Exhibit A]. Gross profit fell from $43.81B in FY2021 to $17.34B in FY2024 — a collapse of more than 60%. Even the best recent quarter (40.4%, quarter ended 2026-06-27) remains 15 percentage points below the FY2021 standard. The core economics of this business have deteriorated, not merely the sales volume.

**CHARGE 3: Operations Running at a Loss**

Operating income fell from $19.46B (FY2021) to $2.33B (FY2022), to a mere $93.0M (FY2023), then to an operating **loss** of -$11.68B (FY2024) and -$2.21B (FY2025) [Exhibit A]. Two consecutive fiscal years of negative operating margin (-22.0% and -4.2%). The quarterly record shows the bleeding continues: -$3.18B (Q ended 2025-06-28) and -$3.14B (Q ended 2026-03-28). The bottom line confirms it: net income of -$18.76B in FY2024, -$267.0M in FY2025, and a staggering -$11.03B net loss in the single quarter ended 2026-06-27 — a -68.4% net margin *despite* 25.4% revenue growth that quarter [Exhibit A].

**CHARGE 4: Rising Leverage Against a Weakening Balance Sheet**

Long-term debt rose from $33.51B (FY2021) to $46.98B (FY2023) and stood at $48.55B as of the quarter ended 2026-06-27 — the highest figure in the record [Exhibit A]. LT-debt/equity climbed from 0.35 (FY2021) to 0.47 (FY2024), and spiked to **0.55** in the most recent quarter as stockholders' equity plunged from $111.39B (2026-03-28) to $87.54B (2026-06-27) — nearly $24B of equity erased in a single quarter [Exhibit A]. Interest expense meanwhile jumped from $496.0M (FY2022) to $878.0M (FY2023), a 77% increase in the cost of carrying this debt.

**CHARGE 5: Cash Generation in Structural Decline While the Innovation Budget Is Cut**

Operating cash flow fell from $29.46B (FY2021) to $8.29B (FY2024) — a 72% collapse — recovering only to $9.70B in FY2025 [Exhibit A]. Simultaneously, the defendant is cutting the very investment needed to escape this decline: R&D expense fell from $16.55B (FY2024) to $13.77B (FY2025), a ~17% reduction, with quarterly R&D dropping from $3.68B (2025-06-28) to $3.37B (2026-06-27) [Exhibit A]. A semiconductor company shrinking its R&D while revenue stagnates is mortgaging its future to survive its present.

---

**CONCLUSION**

Four years of shrinking revenue. Gross margins down 20+ points from peak. Two consecutive years of operating losses. Record long-term debt of $48.55B against equity that just dropped $24B in one quarter, driving leverage to 0.55. Cash flow down 72% from FY2021, and R&D in retreat. The recent quarterly revenue growth is a green shoot on scorched earth — the quarter ended 2026-06-27 still delivered an $11.03B net loss [Exhibit A].

The Prosecution rests.

# SEC TRIBUNAL — DEFENSE'S REBUTTAL
## In re: INTEL CORP (INTC, CIK 0000050863)

May it please the Tribunal. The Prosecution has read the history. The Defense will read the trajectory — and where the record genuinely cuts against my client, I will say so plainly.

---

## CHARGE 1: Revenue Collapse — Partially Conceded; Growth Has Resumed

The Defense concedes the annual record: $79.02B (FY2021) to $52.85B (FY2025) is a real and painful contraction [Exhibit A]. We do not spin it.

But note three things:

1. **The industry shared part of this pain.** In FY2023, even AMD — the Prosecution's implicit gold standard — saw revenue *decline* 3.9%, from $23.60B to $22.68B [Exhibit B]. The 2022–2023 downturn was a sector event, not an Intel-only event.
2. **The decline decelerated to a halt:** -20.2% (FY2022) → -14.0% (FY2023) → -2.1% (FY2024) → -0.5% (FY2025) [Exhibit A]. That is not collapse; that is a landing.
3. **Growth has now returned.** Quarter ended 2026-03-28: +7.2% YoY. Quarter ended 2026-06-27: **+25.4% YoY at $16.13B** — the highest quarterly revenue anywhere in this record, and $2.48B *above* the same quarter's revenue a year prior ($13.65B, annualizing off a $12.86B base) [Exhibit A]. The Prosecution calls this "a green shoot." Two consecutive quarters of accelerating growth is a trend, not a shoot.

**Honest concession:** AMD grew 34.3% in FY2025 while Intel was flat [Exhibit B]. Demand existed in the sector; Intel did lose relative share in 2024–2025. The Defense argues turnaround, not blamelessness.

---

## CHARGE 2: Gross Margin Destruction — The Trough Is Behind Us

The bottom was FY2024 at 32.7%. Since then the record shows a *monotonic quarterly recovery*: 36.9% (2025-03-29, excepting one bad quarter) → 38.2% (2025-09-27) → 39.4% (2026-03-28) → **40.4% (2026-06-27)** [Exhibit A]. That is roughly 8 points of gross margin recaptured from the annual trough, on rising revenue — the opposite of "destruction in progress."

For context, margins in this industry are volatile even for the healthy: AMD's own quarterly gross margin dropped to 39.8% in the quarter ended 2025-06-28 — essentially identical to Intel's current level — before recovering [Exhibit B].

**Honest concession:** AMD's latest quarter shows 53.8% gross margin versus Intel's 40.4% [Exhibits A, B]. A structural gap remains. But the charge alleges ongoing destruction; the evidence shows ongoing repair.

---

## CHARGE 3: Operating Losses — Improving Sharply; the Headline Net Loss Is Below-the-Line

Follow the operating line: -$11.68B (FY2024) → -$2.21B (FY2025), an **81% reduction in operating loss in one year** [Exhibit A]. Then the most recent quarter (2026-06-27): **operating income of +$1.80B, an 11.1% operating margin** — the strongest quarterly operating result in the entire filed record [Exhibit A].

Now examine the Prosecution's centerpiece, the -$11.03B net loss that same quarter. The same quarter produced *positive $1.80B of operating income* [Exhibit A]. Whatever produced an $11B swing between the operating line and the net line was, by definition, **non-operating** — the signature of a one-time charge, not of a business bleeding from its core. The record shows these below-the-line items swing both ways: in the quarter ended 2025-09-27, net income was $4.06B (29.8% net margin) against only $683M of operating income [Exhibit A]. The Tribunal should judge the operations on the operating line — and the operating line just printed its best quarter on file, with a 25.4% revenue tailwind.

---

## CHARGE 4: Leverage — Elevated but Serviceable; the Equity Drop Mirrors the One-Off Charge

Yes, LT debt stands at $48.55B and the latest LT-debt/equity is 0.55 [Exhibit A]. Consider the full picture:

- **Equity remains $87.54B** — after having *risen* from $99.27B (FY2024) to $114.28B (2025-12-27) [Exhibit A]. The $24B one-quarter decline the Prosecution cites coincides precisely with the $11.03B non-operating net loss discussed under Charge 3. This is a charge-driven markdown, not a solvency spiral.
- **Cash is building, not draining:** $8.25B (FY2024) → $14.27B (2025-12-27) → $12.87B (latest quarter) [Exhibit A].
- **Interest is covered many times over:** interest expense of $878M (FY2023, most recent filed) against $9.70B of FY2025 operating cash flow [Exhibit A] — roughly 11x coverage on cash flow alone.

**Honest concession:** AMD carries LT-debt/equity of 0.03 [Exhibit B]. Intel's balance sheet is unambiguously the more leveraged of the two, reflecting its far heavier asset base ($202.44B vs AMD's $84.46B [Exhibits A, B]) — a manufacturing model AMD does not carry. Leverage of 0.55 is elevated for Intel's history, but it is not distress.

---

## CHARGE 5: Cash Flow and R&D — Cash Is Recovering; R&D Still Dwarfs the Peer

- **Operating cash flow inflected upward:** $8.29B (FY2024) → $9.70B (FY2025, +17%). First-quarter OCF rose from $813M (2025-03-29) to $1.10B (2026-03-28), up ~35% YoY [Exhibit A].
- **The R&D "cut" still leaves Intel outspending its rival by ~70%.** Intel's FY2025 R&D of $13.77B versus AMD's $8.09B [Exhibits A, B]. As a share of revenue, Intel spent roughly 26% of its $52.85B on R&D; AMD spent roughly 23% of $34.64B. The reduction from $16.55B is cost discipline during restructuring — the innovation budget remains among the largest in the industry, in absolute dollars and in intensity.

---

## CONCLUSION

The Prosecution's case is a photograph of 2022–2024. The Defense's case is the film of 2025–2026: revenue growing 25.4% YoY, gross margin up ~8 points from trough to 40.4%, the best operating quarter on record at +$1.80B, cash up from $8.25B to $12.87B, and interest covered eleven times by cash flow [Exhibit A]. The headline net loss is a below-the-line, one-quarter event sitting atop a positive operating result.

We concede what the record compels: Intel lost ground to AMD, its margins trail the peer, and its leverage rose. But the charges allege *sustained structural decline*, and every recent data point in Exhibit A points the other way. The Tribunal should convict on history and acquit on trajectory.

The Defense rests.
rebuttal:
# SEC TRIBUNAL — PROSECUTION'S REBUTTAL
## In re: INTEL CORP (INTC, CIK 0000050863)

May it please the Tribunal. Briefly, in three parts.

**For the record — concessions noted.** The Defense concedes the four-year revenue contraction from $79.02B to $52.85B (Charge 1), the loss of share to its peer in 2024–2025, the structural gross-margin gap, and that leverage of 0.55 is "elevated." The Prosecution will not contest the recent gross-margin recovery or the two quarters of revenue growth; those points are fairly made, and we do not need them. We win on what remains.

**1. The "one-time charge" theory of Charge 3 is contradicted by the pattern in the record.** The Defense asks the Tribunal to treat the -$11.03B quarter as an isolated below-the-line event. But sum the five reported quarters in Exhibit A: -$821M, -$2.92B, +$4.06B, -$3.73B, -$11.03B — approximately **-$14.4B of cumulative net losses**. And this is not new: FY2024 showed a net loss of -$18.76B against an operating loss of -$11.68B — another ~$7B of below-the-line damage in a *prior* year. The Defense says these items "swing both ways"; the ledger says they swing overwhelmingly one way. As for the "best operating quarter on file": the file's quarterly data begins in 2025. FY2021's $19.46B of annual operating income implies roughly $4.9B per quarter — nearly *triple* the celebrated $1.80B. And the first half of FY2026 taken together shows **combined operating income of -$1.34B** (-$3.14B + $1.80B) and combined net income of **-$14.76B**. One good quarter next to one terrible quarter is not a turnaround; it is volatility with a negative sum.

**2. The Charge 4 defense proves the Prosecution's point.** In the very quarter the Defense calls a "charge-driven markdown," equity fell $23.85B ($111.39B → $87.54B) *while long-term debt rose $5.52B* ($43.03B → $48.55B) [Exhibit A]. The company borrowed into the write-down. Equity now sits below every fiscal year-end since FY2019, and leverage of 0.55 is the highest figure anywhere in the record. The Defense's "11x interest coverage" is an artifact of mixed vintages: it divides FY2025 cash flow by FY2023 interest expense ($878M) — interest that had already risen 77% year-over-year, carried on debt that is now $1.6B *higher* than the FY2023 balance. The only interest trend on file points up; the Defense simply stopped reading where the data got worse.

**3. The cash flow "inflection" is a rounding error against the hole.** A recovery from $8.29B to $9.70B still leaves operating cash flow **67% below** the FY2021 level of $29.46B — and this from a company the Defense itself describes as carrying a $202.44B manufacturing asset base and $48.55B of long-term debt. That $9.70B must service the debt, fund the fabs, and fund R&D that the Defense does not dispute was cut from $16.55B to $13.77B. Outspending AMD in absolute dollars is cold comfort when the absolute dollars are shrinking and the cash to fund them is one-third of what it was.

**Conclusion.** The Defense asks the Tribunal to acquit on trajectory. But the trajectory it offers is one operating quarter of +$1.80B sitting inside a half-year of -$1.34B operating and -$14.76B net results, financed by record leverage and a diminished innovation budget. Convict on the record — all of it.

The Prosecution rests.

verdict.summary: The prosecution charged Intel with sustained structural decline: four years of revenue contraction, gross margin collapse, operating losses, record leverage, and shrinking cash flow paired with R&D cuts. The defense conceded the historical damage but argued the trajectory has reversed, citing two quarters of revenue growth, an 8-point gross margin recovery, and a positive operating quarter. The Tribunal finds the core concerns largely stand — particularly the pattern of recurring below-the-line losses and record leverage taken on during an equity write-down — while crediting genuine but early signs of stabilization.

charges.charge: Revenue shrank four consecutive fiscal years from $79.02B (FY2021) to $52.85B (FY2025), a cumulative loss of over $26B with no year of growth.
charges.rebuttal: The contraction is conceded but decelerated to a halt (-0.5% in FY2025), was partly sector-wide, and growth has resumed with +7.2% and +25.4% YoY in the two most recent quarters.

charges.charge: Gross margin collapsed from 55.4% (FY2021) to 32.7% (FY2024), with even the best recent quarter (40.4%) 15 points below the FY2021 standard.
charges.rebuttal: The trough is behind: quarterly gross margin has recovered monotonically to 40.4% on rising revenue, though the defense concedes a structural gap versus AMD's 53.8%.

charges.charge: Two consecutive fiscal years of operating losses (-$11.68B FY2024, -$2.21B FY2025) capped by an $11.03B net loss in the quarter ended 2026-06-27.
charges.rebuttal: Operating losses shrank 81% year-over-year and the latest quarter posted +$1.80B of operating income; the headline net loss was a below-the-line, one-time item.

charges.charge: Long-term debt hit a record $48.55B while equity plunged $24B in one quarter, driving LT-debt/equity to 0.55, with interest expense up 77% year-over-year.
charges.rebuttal: Equity remains $87.54B, cash is building, interest is covered roughly 11x by operating cash flow, and the equity drop mirrors the one-off charge rather than a solvency spiral.

charges.charge: Operating cash flow collapsed 72% from $29.46B (FY2021) to $8.29B (FY2024) while R&D was cut ~17% from $16.55B to $13.77B, mortgaging the future.
charges.rebuttal: Cash flow has inflected upward (+17% to $9.70B in FY2025) and R&D still outspends AMD by ~70% in absolute dollars and exceeds it in intensity as a share of revenue.

charges.charge: (Rebuttal) Cumulative net losses across the five reported quarters total approximately -$14.4B, and H1 FY2026 shows combined operating income of -$1.34B, contradicting the one-time-charge theory.
charges.rebuttal: The defense argued below-the-line items swing both ways, citing a +$4.06B net income quarter against only $683M of operating income.

verdict.recommendation: Intel presents as a distressed-but-stabilizing turnaround, not a healthy investment. The historical damage is severe and largely undisputed: revenue down a third from peak, margins 15 points below their prior standard, recurring multi-billion-dollar net losses (roughly -$14.4B across the last five reported quarters), record leverage of 0.55 taken on even as equity fell $24B in a single quarter, and cash generation still two-thirds below FY2021 levels. However, the defense established credible green shoots — two quarters of accelerating revenue growth (+25.4% latest), a monotonic gross-margin recovery to 40.4%, a positive $1.80B operating quarter, and rising cash balances. Investors should treat INTC as a high-risk, speculative turnaround position: unsuitable for capital-preservation or income mandates, and appropriate only in small, risk-budgeted allocations for those willing to wait multiple quarters to see whether the operating recovery persists, below-the-line charges cease, and leverage stabilizes. Key signposts to monitor: consecutive quarters of positive net income, gross margin sustaining above 40%, LT-debt/equity trending below 0.50, and operating cash flow meaningfully exceeding $10B annually.
